data.name: Phyllys
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Phyllys was a nymph who dedicated her life to protecting and caring for the gods. In Christianity, the name Phyllys represents the idea of being a devoted servant of God, a daughter of God, and a protector of the faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and devotion to God.
data.numerology_meaning: Those with the life path number 2 are natural peacemakers and nurturers. They have a strong desire for harmony, love, and beauty, and a great talent for creating a pleasant atmosphere.
data.cultural_impact: In Greek mythology, the name Phyllys was linked to the meaning "to shine." While this meaning may not hold much significance in the Christian context, the name has been used throughout history by Christians as a testament to their faith and devotion. Phyllys can also be considered a derivative of the Greek word "phylax," which means "protector" - a role that aligns perfectly with the Christian idea of being a servant of God and a steward of faith.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Phyllys signifies dedication, purity, and protection. As a servant of God, Phyllys embodies the virtues of faithfulness, love, and obedience to God's will. Her name can serve as a reminder to Christians of their role as protectors of the faith, caretakers of their own spiritual growth, and stewards of the gifts and talents that they've been given. Through the name Phyllys, Christians can be encouraged to foster a deep, personal relationship with God, to lean on Him for strength and guidance, and to extend His love and care to others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Phyllys is mentioned in the works of the historian Suetonius. The name Phyllys carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Phyllys is associated with the Roman Empire and is likely of Latin origin.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Phyllys remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
